title: Health insurance in Germany: clarifying your coverage
intro: People living in Germany generally need health insurance. Statutory and private systems have different eligibility, contributions and reimbursement arrangements. This overview cannot decide individual entitlement, particularly for newcomers, temporary visitors or people with uncertain coverage.

sections.heading: Establish eligibility
paragraphs: Establish your situation before choosing: employment, study, family membership, self-employment and previous insurance can matter. Ask an insurer or independent adviser which rules apply. Do not assume travel insurance or a European card replaces the cover required for long-term residence.

sections.heading: Compare coverage and costs
paragraphs: Compare covered services, contributions, dependants, co-payments and possible up-front bills. Statutory contributions and private premiums follow different principles; an initially attractive price does not show the lifetime cost or ease of switching back.

sections.heading: Check planned services
paragraphs: Before a planned private service, ask whether it is covered and obtain clear information about charges and alternatives. For expensive treatment or aids, check whether prior approval is needed. Keep written decisions and ask how to seek review if coverage is refused.

sections.heading: Changes and gaps in coverage
paragraphs: If insurance lapses or your circumstances change, contact the insurer promptly. Ask for understandable written steps, language support and independent advice where needed. Clarify children’s coverage separately and keep proof available, rather than assuming every family member is automatically included.

sections.heading: Emergencies and current rules
paragraphs: Serious symptoms still require urgent medical help; do not delay an emergency to resolve paperwork. Arrange a separate discussion about coverage and billing. Current financial thresholds and entitlement rules can change, so verify them before signing or cancelling a policy.

examples.title: A practical example
examples.text: In this hypothetical example, Mira starts a new job and asks when her cover begins and whether her child is included. She obtains written confirmation instead of relying on an informal promise.

examples.title: Another practical example
examples.text: In this hypothetical example, Arben is offered an optional paid examination. He asks about medical purpose, insurance coverage and cost before agreeing, without assuming every offered test is compulsory.

questions: Which insurance rules apply to my circumstances?
What is covered and which charges may remain?
Where can I obtain independent advice or review?
